## Problem 1
```{r setup, message=FALSE, echo=FALSE}
library(p8105.datasets)
library(patchwork)
library(tidyverse)

library(knitr)
options(digits = 2)
data("ny_noaa")
```

```{r}
noaa_df = ny_noaa %>% 
  janitor::clean_names()

na_count <- noaa_df %>%
  summarize(across(everything(), ~ mean(is.na(.)) * 100 ))
```

This dataframe contains `r nrow(noaa_df)` rows and `r ncol(noaa_df)` columns. The key variables include date, prcp (the amount of precipitation that day, in tenths of mm) snow (in mm), snwd (depth of the snow that day, in mm) tmax and tmin (the maximum and minimum temperatures that day in tenths of degrees C). Missing data is an issue here, as every weather station does not collect every value. Accordingly, `r pull(na_count, snow)`% of the snow data, `r pull(na_count, snwd)`% of snow depth, and `r pull(na_count, tmin)`% of both temp min and temp max data are missing.


```{r}
noaa_df = noaa_df %>% 
  mutate(
    day = lubridate::day(date),
    month = lubridate::month(date),
    year = lubridate::year(date),
    snow = ifelse(
      snow < 0, NA, snow
    ),
    prcp = prcp / 10,
    tmin = as.numeric(tmin) / 10,
    tmax = as.numeric(tmax) / 10
  )

noaa_df %>% 
  count(snow, name = "n_obs") %>% 
  arrange(desc(n_obs))

head(noaa_df)
```
We add day, month, and year columns. Snow values less than 0 were changed to be NAs. We then adjust the prcp, tmax, and tmin to be full mm and degrees C, respectively. The majority of counts for snowfall were 0, since it does not snow in most places on most days.

```{r}
ggp_monthly_temp = noaa_df %>%
  filter(
    month %in% c(1, 7)
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    month = ifelse(
      month == 1, "January", "July"
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(id, month, year) %>%
  summarize(
    avg_max = mean(tmax)
  )  %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = avg_max)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~ month, ncol = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "Average Temperature by Station and Month",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Average Monthly Temperature (C)"
  )
  
ggp_monthly_temp
```
The plots of average temperatures in January and July show relatively consistent temperatures, with a few outliers (e.g. one very cold day in July in the late 1980s).

```{r}
ggp_full_tmp = noaa_df %>%
  pivot_longer(
    tmax:tmin,
    names_to = "observation", 
    values_to = "temp") %>%  
  ggplot(aes(x = temp, fill = observation)) +
  geom_density(alpha = .5) +
  labs(
    title = "Average Temperature by Station and Month",
    x = "Temperature (C)",
    y = "Density"
  )

ggp_snowfall = noaa_df %>% 
  filter(
    snow > 0 & snow < 100
  ) %>% 
  count(year, name = "snow_count") %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y=snow_count)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    title = "Snowfall Amounts",
    x = "# of Snowfalls between 0 and 100mm",
    y = "Year"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position="none")
  

ggp_full_tmp + ggp_snowfall
```

We made two density plots. The left compares minimum and maximum temperature by station and month, while the right shows how often stations recorded days with snowfalls between 0 and 100 millimeters by year.

## Problem 2
```{r}
accel_df = read.csv("./files/nhanes_accel.csv") %>% 
  janitor::clean_names() %>% 
  pivot_longer(
    min1:min1440,
    names_to = "minute", 
    values_to = "mims"
    )
covar_df = read.csv("./files/nhanes_covar.csv", skip = 4) %>% 
  janitor::clean_names() %>% 
  mutate(
    sex = as.factor(ifelse(sex == 1, "Male", "Female")), 
    education = as.factor(recode_values(
      education,
        1 ~ "Less than high school",
        2 ~ "High school",
        3 ~ "More than high school"
      ))
  )

mims_df = accel_df %>% 
  left_join(covar_df, 'seqn')

head(mims_df)
```

We load and tidy the datasets, pivoting the minutes into their own rows for the acceleration csv and changing from codes to male and female. We then left join them on the 'seqn' column. 

```{r}
mims_df = mims_df %>% 
  filter(age >= 21) %>%
  group_by(seqn) %>% 
  filter(!any(if_any(everything(), is.na))) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(
    education = as.factor(education),
    minute = as.numeric(str_remove(minute, "^min"))
  )
head(mims_df)
```

Education and minute are changed to factors, and rows for people under 21 years old are removed. We also remove any participants with na values.

```{r}
education_table <- mims_df %>%
  count(education, sex) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = sex,
    values_from = n,
    values_fill = 0
  ) %>%
  mutate(Total = Male + Female) %>%
  arrange(education)

kable(
  education_table,
  col.names = c("Education", "Men", "Women", "Total")
)

```

We create a chart with education levels by sex, along with totals. The largest category is More than high school. 

```{r}
ggplot(
  mims_df,
  aes(x = sex, y = age, fill = sex)
) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ education) +
  labs(
    title = "Age Distribution by Sex and Education",
    x = "Sex",
    y = "Age (years)",
    fill = "Sex"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```

The people with more than a high school education are generally younger than the other education levels. Among people with a high school education, the females with  were older than the males.  

```{r}
activity_totals <- mims_df %>%
  group_by(seqn, sex, age, education) %>%
  summarize(
    total_activity = sum(mims),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(activity_totals,
       aes(x = age, y = total_activity, color = sex)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(~ education) +
  labs(
    title = "Total Activity by Age, Sex, and Education",
    x = "Age (years)",
    y = "Total Activity (MIMS)",
    color = "Sex"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

As age increases, total activity decreases across all education levels and sexes. Women tended to do more activity than men for groups with at least a high school education, while the opposite was generally true for people with less than a high school education. 

```{r}
activity_by_minute <- mims_df %>%
  group_by(education, sex, minute) %>%
  summarize(
    mean_mims = mean(mims),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(activity_by_minute,
       aes(x = minute / 60,
           y = mean_mims)) +
  geom_line(
    linewidth = 0.8,
    aes(color = sex),
    alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(
    aes(color = sex), 
    method = "loess",
    span = 0.08,
    se = FALSE,
    linewidth = 1.2
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Male" = "#1565C0", "Female" = "#E65100")) +
  facet_wrap(~ education, ncol = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 24, by = 4),
    limits = c(0, 24)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "24-Hour Activity Patterns by Education and Sex",
    x = "Time of Day (Hours)",
    y = "Mean Activity (MIMS)",
    color = "Sex"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```

The plots of 24 hour activity show low activity in the early morning, with generally sustained energy throughout the middle of the day and into the night. 

## Problem 3

```{r message=FALSE}
jan_2020_citi_df <- read.csv("./files/Jan 2020 Citi.csv") %>%   
  janitor::clean_names()
jan_2024_citi_df <- read_csv("./files/Jan 2024 Citi.csv") %>%   
  janitor::clean_names()
jul_2020_citi_df <- read_csv("./files/July 2020 Citi.csv") %>%   
  janitor::clean_names()
jul_2024_citi_df <- read_csv("./files/July 2024 Citi.csv") %>%   
  janitor::clean_names()

citi_df <- bind_rows(
  jan_2020_citi_df %>% mutate(year = 2020, month = "January"),
  jan_2024_citi_df %>% mutate(year = 2024, month = "January"),
  jul_2020_citi_df %>% mutate(year = 2020, month = "July"),
  jul_2024_citi_df %>% mutate(year = 2024, month = "July")
) %>%
  mutate(
    month = factor(month, levels = c("January", "July")),
    member_casual = factor(member_casual,
                           levels = c("casual", "member"),
                           labels = c("Casual", "Member")),
    year = factor(year)
  )

head(citi_df)
```

We import the 4 csv files, add columns for year and month, then bind them into one dataframe. We turn month, membership, and year into factors. We end up with a dataframe of `r nrow(citi_df)` rows and `rncol(citi)` columns. The rows indicate a single rental of a bike, and the columns are ride id, rideable type (classic or ebike), day of the week, ride duration, the starting and ending station, membership of the rider, year, and month.

```{r}
ride_counts <- citi_df %>%
  count(year, month, member_casual) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = member_casual,
    values_from = n,
    values_fill = 0
  ) %>%
  mutate(Total = Casual + Member) %>%
  arrange(year, month)

kable(
  ride_counts,
  caption = "Total Citi Bike Rides by Year, Month, and Membership",
  col.names = c("Year", "Month", "Casual Riders",
                "Members", "Total Rides"),
  format.args = list(big.mark = ",")
)
```

There are more rides in July each year than in January. Ridership has increased between 2020 and 2024 in both January and July. Most rides are by citibike members. Members make up a much larger proportion of total rides in January of both years than they do in July.

```{r}
top_stations <- jul_2024_citi_df %>%
  filter(!is.na(start_station_name),
         start_station_name != "") %>%
  count(start_station_name, sort = TRUE) %>%
  slice_head(n = 5) %>%
  rename(
    "Starting Station" = start_station_name,
    "Number of Rides" = n
  )

kable(
  top_stations,
  caption = "Five Most Popular Citi Bike Starting Stations, July 2024",
  format.args = list(big.mark = ",")
)
```

```{r}
median_duration <- citi_df %>%
  mutate(
    weekdays = factor(
      weekdays,
      levels = c("Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday",
                 "Thursday", "Friday", "Saturday", "Sunday")
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(duration), duration >= 0,
         !is.na(weekdays)) %>%
  group_by(year, month, weekdays) %>%
  summarize(
    median_duration = median(duration),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(median_duration,
       aes(x = weekdays,
           y = median_duration,
           color = year,
           group = year)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~ month) +
  scale_x_discrete(
    labels = c("Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu",
               "Fri", "Sat", "Sun")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Median Citi Bike Ride Duration",
    subtitle = "Comparison by Weekday, Month, and Year",
    x = "Day of Week",
    y = "Median Ride Duration",
    color = "Year"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Generally speaking, people take longer rides on the weekend (besides Sundays in January 2024). People took longer rides in 2020 than in 2024, and July also has longer rides than January. 

```{r}

citi_2024 <- citi_df %>%
  filter(
    year == "2024",
    !is.na(duration),
    duration > 0,
    !is.na(rideable_type),
    !is.na(member_casual)
  )

ggplot(citi_2024,
       aes(x = member_casual,
           y = duration,
           fill = rideable_type)) +
  geom_boxplot(
    outlier.shape = NA,
    alpha = 0.75
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ month) +
  coord_cartesian(
    ylim = c(0, quantile(citi_2024$duration, 0.95))
  ) +
  scale_fill_discrete(
    labels = c(
      "classic_bike" = "Classic Bike",
      "electric_bike" = "Electric Bike"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Citi Bike Ride Duration Distributions in 2024",
    subtitle = "Comparison by Month, Membership, and Bike Type",
    x = "Membership Status",
    y = "Ride Duration",
    fill = "Bike Type"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Casual (non-member) riders take longer riddes on classic bikes than on ebikes, while the opposite is true for members. Members have shorter rides than casual riders, perhaps indicating they aren't taking joyrides.
